Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to stay afloat as Fifa president after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support.

England, Wales and other European nations have led the charge in officially withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027, while Uefa asserted that its boycott of Fifa competitions still stands in a bid to oust him from power.

The global players union, Fifpro, have also turned on Infantino, accusing him of a “profound abuse of presidential power” in an explosive statement.

However, Infantino’s allies are beginning to surface, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf, the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president.

As dominoes continue to fall, here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino:

Who has withdrawn its support for Infantino?

Uefa 🇪🇺

Uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership, insisting that its boycott of Fifa competitions still stands despite the sell-off scheme being scrapped.

It points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”.

The French Football Federation, however, have indicated to BBC Sport that they still intend to compete at next month’s U20 Women’s World Cup despite the confederation-wide boycott.

England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿

The English FA are one of many European member associations to send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election in 2027.

Infantino’s apology letter that was sent around on Wednesday night changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding his sell-off scheme.

open image in gallery FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) next to Gianni Infantino ( PA )

Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿

The Football Association of Wales were one of the first to send its letter withdrawing support for Infantino.

“The ‌recent failures in good governance, processes, ‌leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment ​have led us to a position ‌where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to ‌remain at the helm of world football,” a statement read. “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.”

Finland 🇫🇮

Finland kickstarted this process, with it being revealed that the Scandinavian member association was the first to send a letter officially withdrawing support for Infantino.

Serbia 🇷🇸

The Football Association of Serbia then sent a similar letter to Fifa.

“We would like to remind you that we provided our support to Mr Infantino in writing on 25 May of this year, but after carefully considering the events that have seriously damaged the image and reputation of both Fifa and its president in the past period, this is the only logical and rational course of action,” a statement read.

Sweden 🇸🇪

Sweden’s federation (SvFF) followed suit: "At an extraordinary board meeting on Monday, SvFF has chosen not to support Fifa President Gianni Infantino ​in the upcoming re-election.

"This is after a long-term assessment of the development within Fifa and the organization's leadership. The decision is based on recurring shortcomings in governance, transparency and management, which means that trust in Gianni Infantino's leadership no longer exists."

open image in gallery Infantino has officially lost the endorsement of numerous Uefa nations ( PA )

Croatia 🇭🇷

As did the Croatian Football Federation (HNS): "The Croatian Football Federation has informed Fifa of its decision to withdraw the support previously expressed for Mr Gianni Infantino's candidature for another term as Fifa president.

"This decision followed a thorough reassessment within the federation in light of recent developments surrounding the Fifa World Cup 2026 and discussions within our governing bodies. We consider our position to be clearly communicated to Fifa and have no further comment to add at this time."

Albania 🇦🇱

The Albanian Football Federation also took the same stance, aligning with Uefa.

“The Albanian Football Association has sent an official letter to Fifa Secretary General Mattias Grafström, informing him that it has withdrawn its support for Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for another four-year term as Fifa President,” the statement confirmed.

Greece 🇬🇷

The Greek federation similarly sent their withdrawal of support Fifa’s way.

Who is also opposing Infantino?

Concacaf (Confederation for North America and the Caribbean) 🌎

Concacaf have come out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off plan, which they went on to reject.

After the plan was aborted, the confederation said: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.”

It also wrote a joint statement with Uefa and the AFC which intended to give Infantino the opportunity to resign with dignity.

Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is widely being seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election.

open image in gallery Concacaf president Victor Montagliani is widely being seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino ( Getty )

AFC (Asian Football Confederation) 🌏

The AFC was similarly aggrieved by the non-existent consultation from Fifa regarding the Infantino’s scheme, rejecting the proposal before calling on Fifa to undertake an “urgent review of its governance”.

The confederation’s part in a joint statement with Uefa and Concacaf confirms their desire to see Infantino ousted from power.

Germany 🇩🇪

The German federation (DFB) already opted against endorsing Infantino earlier in the year so has not had to send a letter withdrawing support to take an opposing stance.

“The DFB has not signed a letter of support for the re-election of Gianni Infantino," the governing body stated in July. "Further steps will be discussed in the DFB presidential board."

Denmark 🇩🇰

Denmark are in a similar position to Germany, having not endorsed Infantino’s re-election bid prior to the scheme’s reveal.

There is also a precedent for their opposition to Infantino, with federation president Jesper Moller not supporting his re-election efforts back in 2022: “There is only one candidate ... but Denmark will not be supporting the current president.”

Norway 🇳🇴

The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) have been one of the most vocal bodies to call for Infantino’s resignation, and while they have not yet officially sent a letter to withdraw their support in him, such action is expected in the coming days.

NFF president Lise Klaveness told the Guardian: “We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now. We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.

“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”

open image in gallery Lise Klaveness has called on Infantino to resign ( Reuters )

Netherlands 🇳🇱

The Royal Dutch Football Association (KNVB) is also yet to officially withdraw its support but is among the many to have confirmed it has lost confidence in Infantino’s leadership.

“The way this process has unfolded has resulted in a fundamental loss of confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino. The KNVB no longer has confidence in his leadership,” a statement read.

Romania 🇷🇴

The Romanian Football Federation (FRF) were among the countries to resolutely reject the sell-off proposal, calling it “a dangerous initiative to turn football into a private asset.

As a result, the FRF will withold support for Infantino’s re-election for the time being, with a statement reading: “FRF is suspending the discussion regarding the support of Fifa President Gianni Infantino for a new term, until further clarifications.”

Jordan 🇯🇴

Jordan are so far the only non-Uefa member association to publicly oppose Infantino after federation president Prince Ali bin Hussein levelled accusations of blackmail against Fifa.

Prince Ali alleged the organisation offered assistance with the kingdom's issues in exchange for his endorsement, following Infantino's withdrawal from a World Cup stake sale proposal. Among the problems cited was the association's eight-month wait for prize money, due since December for reaching the Arab Cup final in Qatar.

After taking to X to reveal the outstanding payments, the Jordan Football Association received the prize money two days later - but Prince Ali has not changed his stance over not endorsing Infantino: “It does not change my clear position concerning the leadership of Fifa: my FA and I will not endorse president Infantino, nor will we vote for him.”

Sierra Leone 🇸🇱

Former Sierra Leone FA president and ex-Fifa Council member Isha Johansen has indicated that Africa’s support of Infantino is not unanimous across the continent after emerging as one of the African voices opposing the privatisation project.

He urged African football chiefs to think carefully about the game’s future, saying: "What price does one have to pay in order to get to this elevated development for football in Africa?"

Canada 🇨🇦

Canada prime minister Mark Carney joined his UK counterpart Andy Burnham in calling for Infantino to be ousted from his position as president.

“It should be fatal,” Carney said, whose country co-hosted this summer’s World Cup. “Certainly I don’t have confidence in Mr Infantino."

However, the country has confirmed it will not boycott Fifa competitions and participate in the U20 Women’s World Cup in Poland.

Who is supporting Infantino?

Caf (African Football Confederation) 🌍

Caf, the governing body for African football, has become the first confederation to unanimously back Infantino. Its 54 member associations account more than a quarter of Fifa’s 211 members.

“We are committed to continue working together with Fifa, its member associations, other football confederations and stakeholders to safeguard and adhere to governance, due process, and transparency global best practises and to contribute to the development and growth of football worldwide,” Caf president Patrice Motsepe said.

Motsepe later added thar the position of embattled president Infantino can only be decided by Fifa elections.

Argentina 🇦🇷

Argentina became the first member from South America to voice its support for Infantino, on the same day that confederation Conmebol - which had thus far only expressed support of Infantino - expressed concern over Fifa’s procedures.

"Of our highest consideration, on behalf of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), and its Executive Committee, we address you, dear President, and through your worthy intermediary the Fifa board, to express our support for the management carried out during the last 10 years, which had as its main axes the development of football throughout the world and institutional solidity based on a clear governance model, stable and transparent,” a statement read.

open image in gallery Argentina president Javier Milei (left) behind Infantino at the "Board of Peace" hosted by US president Donald Trump ( AFP/Getty )

Mexico 🇲🇽

Mexico joined Argentina from the Americas, breaking rank from the United States, Canada and the rest of Concacaf that had condemned Infantino’s plan and aligned itself against his leadership.

The Mexican Football Federation (FMF) stated: "The FMF will neither recognise nor approve any process convened outside of that institutional framework, and it joins the call made... by President Infantino to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of the 211 member associations."

Paraguay 🇵🇾

Paraguay has also followed suit as Infantino’s Conmebol support base begins to surface.

Their federation published a letter of support addressed to Infantino, writing that it "reaffirms its commitment to continue working alongside Fifa”.

Qatar 🇶🇦

Qatar was the first football association to publicly back Infantino, even though they later welcomed the decision to scrap the plan.

"While the proposal had merit, we applaud the wisdom behind prioritising unity among member associations. The Qatar Football Association fully supports President Infantino's efforts to continue growing and strengthening the game globally,” a statement read.

open image in gallery Qatar's FA has backed Infantino to continue as president ( Getty Images )

Sri Lanka 🇱🇰

Like Qatar, Sri Lanka welcomed the decision to scrap the investment plan and has since reaffirmed its support for Infantino.

"One of President Infantino's defining leadership qualities has always been his willingness to listen to the views and concerns of Member Associations. This decision is a clear reflection of his inclusive leadership style, built on dialogue, mutual respect, and a genuine commitment to serving the global football community," its statement read.

Kuwait 🇰🇼

Like others, Kuwait welcomed the decision to halt the plans but Sheikh Ahmed Yusuf Al-Sabah, the president of the Kuwait Football Association, affirmed his support for Infantino.

A statement read: “He concluded by affirming the Kuwait Football Association's confidence in the leadership of Fifa President Gianni Infantino, and its support for efforts aimed at developing the game and enhancing its opportunities for growth in a way that serves all national associations and achieves the shared interests of global football.”

Lebanon 🇱🇧

Lebanon, who granted Infantino citizenship last year, have backed the Swiss-Italian, with FA president Hashim Haidar all but echoing the same sentiments as Kuwait.

“Haidar reaffirms the Lebanese Football Association’s support for Fifa President Gianni Infantino and his confidence in the decisions he makes in the best interests of global football, as well as in his efforts and initiatives aimed at developing the game,” he said, while also asserting that Infantino’s proposal “could be re-examined ... in a away that serves the greater good of the sport and preserves its unity”.

Indonesia 🇮🇩

The president of the Indonesian FA supported Infantino’s sell-off plan and has now backed him for another term.

Hailing Fifa as a “strategic partner that is truly present” in its football development, Erick Thohir said: “This is proof of President Infantino’s vision that football development must not be centered on a single region; it must proceed worldwide.”

Philippines 🇵🇭

Philippines have also backed Infantino and backed for co-operation among confederations.

"We stand behind President Gianni Infantino's leadership, and trust that continued dialogue among all confederations and member associations will keep the global game moving forward together,” the Philippines confirmed.

Mongolia 🇲🇳

Joining the Philippines, the Mongolian Football Federation has put out a statement in support of Infantino.

Bhutan 🇧🇹

The Bhutan Football Federation has published a letter that extends its “sincere appreciation” to Infantino for scrapping the plans, hailing him for demonstrating “true leadership” by “prioritising consensus over commerce”.

“We stand united with Fifa and President Infantino in their ongoing efforts to serve the global football community,” wrote federation president Dasho Ugen Tsechup.

Morocco 🇲🇦

The location of Infantino’s crisis meeting on Wednesday, Morocco have stuck by the Swiss-Italian as one of his most loyal allies.

“What has been achieved in recent years through Fifa’s development programmes, particularly in Africa, represents an important accomplishment that must be preserved, to the benefit of all member associations,” said the Royal Moroccan Football Federation’s president Fouzi Lekjaa.

open image in gallery Infantino held his crisis meeting in Rabat, Morocco ( AP )

Egypt 🇪🇬

Similar to their north African counterpart, Egypt have maintained their endorsement of Infantino.

"The Egyptian Football Association reiterates its full trust in President Gianni Infantino's leadership and its continuous support for any initiatives that benefit Fifa member associations and the future of world football,” a statement read.

Mauritania 🇲🇷

Ahmed Yahya, the country's representative on the Fifa Council, was one of a number of African football leaders to say he was backing Infantino early on, pledging his support before Caf took its stance.

Niger 🇳🇪

Same as above, with Hamidou Djibrilla from Niger coming out quickly in support of Infantino.

Sudan 🇸🇩

Sudan’s federation joined five other Arab nations - Qatar, Lebanon, Morocco, Egypt and Mauritania - in writing a joint statement backing Infantino.

"Recognising the important role of Arab football in bringing people together and strengthening co-operation among football associations across the Arab world, we ... express our full support for Mr Gianni Infantino, president of Fifa, and reaffirm our confidence in his leadership and continued commitment to the development of football worldwide," the statement read.

"We deeply appreciate Mr Infantino’s sustained efforts to advance football globally, expand opportunities across all regions and strengthen the game’s role in bringing people and communities together. We look forward to continuing our close cooperation with him towards a stronger and more prosperous future for world ‌football, expanding opportunities and further enhancing Arab football’s contribution to ​the global game."

DR Congo 🇨🇩

DR Congo's federation (Fecofa) president Veron Mosengo-Omba, who was only elected in May, spoke out in “full support”. of Infantino. The two studied at university in Switzerland together.

Fecofa said it had "greatly benefited" from Fifa's programmes, citing investment in development and infrastructure.

Nigeria 🇳🇬

The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has largely aligned itself towards a supportive stance for Infantino's leadership, with former NFF president and deputy chairman of Fifa's Men's National Teams Competitions Committee, Amaju Pinnick, backing his initial sell-off plan.

Comoros 🇰🇲

The president of the Comoros Football Federation, Said Ali Athouman, also backed Infantino’s scheme due to the financial benefits to smaller nations.

"Our problem is how to obtain money,” he said. “Right now, we have no sponsors. So how do we compete? The richest nations can train players, have infrastructure and equipment, and it's no coincidence that they then achieve results. Most European countries don't have ​these problems.”

open image in gallery A number of African nations have fallen in line with the stance of Caf president Patrice Motsepe ( Getty )

Malawi 🇲🇼

Fleetwood Haiya, Malawi's football chief, echoed the same concerns in his support for Infantino.

He told BBC Sport: "Our government is not able to make sure that they have medical supplies in hospitals and at the same time to look at football. Malawi needs money."

Uganda 🇺🇬

The Ugandan federation are said to have echoed Malawi’s sentiments, with football officials from the federation telling BBC Sport that Fifa investment has transformed their game both on and off the pitch.

Gambia 🇬🇲

Lamin Kaba Bajo told BBC Sport that his federation not just stood by Infantino, but would do "everything within our means" to get him re-elected.

"That's my personal opinion as president of the federation, and a good number of African memberships also stand on that line. He is here to stay,” he said.

Djibouti 🇩🇯

The Djiboutian Football Federation has similarly welcomed the decision to withdraw the sell-off proposal, with president Souleiman Hassan Waberi saying the climbdown “demonstrates a firm commitment to preserving the unity, solidarity and cohesion that define the football family”.

He said in a statement: “I reaffirm my full support for Fifa President Mr Gianni Infantino and for all initiatives aimed at promoting the sustainable, transparent and inclusive development of football around the world.”

South Africa 🇿🇦

While not an official statement from the federation, South Africa’s Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture of South Africa, Gayton McKenzie, posted on X saying that Infantino had been "very good to African football".

"Africa should be cautious in joining the public lynching of Infantino,” he warned. “He has been very good to African football. We can debate his ideas but let's not forget who has been a friend to us. Many of those calling for his head want the old status quo back too."

Who are yet to confirm a stance?

The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) has not publicly stated its position, though its biggest footballing nation New Zealand did come out in opposition to Infantino’s proposal. New Zealand have, however, vowed to play at the U20 Women’s World Cup.

Conmebol, the governing body for South America, also took a while to break its silence. It expressed “concern about the repeated unilateral actions taken” and welcomed the decision to withdraw the plans, affirming it will “not support any action” that “ignores or deviates” from the “democratic procedures that represent the 211 Fifa member associations”. However, it is believed the confederation will continue to back Infantino having previously been very supportive of the incumbent president, with Conmebol pushing for a 64-team World Cup for the 2030 edition.

Podcaster Vogue Williams has called out Red Hot Chili Peppers frontman Anthony Kiedis for previously dating a 19-year-old while he was 50.

The musician started dating Australian model Helena Vestergaard in 2013, and they split after being together for approximately two years.

Before that, Kiedis, now 63, had a relationship with Heather Christie, who was 22 years his junior. When the pair welcomed their son, Everly Bear, in 2007, Kiedis was 44 and his partner was 21.

In the latest episode of My Therapist Ghosted Me, Williams and her co-host Joanne McNally discussed age-gap relationships, with the former I’m a Celebrity campmate saying: “Do you know who else I find really disappointing, because I really like the Red Hot Chili Peppers? Anthony Kiedis.”

Seemingly referring to his romance with Vestergaard, Williams continued: “He is like 54 or something, and he is going out with a 19-year-old. And it is like, ‘Dude, what are you talking about?’”

open image in gallery Kiedis with Vestergaard in 2013 ( Getty )

McNally replied: “I've seen this. I just accept now that most men, all men, are drawn to – I'm going to be very careful how I say this – significantly younger women. That's all I'm going to say. It is what it is and I don't think there's any getting away from it. We judge it but it's not going to change.”

“I would have to say that it is not all men,” Williams continued. “Because I do think it is a very specific thing.”

Addressing why younger women might decide to date older men, McNally added: “And of course, people like him [Anthony Kiedis] and rockstars like him can get away with it because no 19-year-old girl wants to be going out with some old lad who is driving a Toyota Corolla around town.

open image in gallery Red Hot Chili Peppers frontman Anthony Kiedis ( Getty )

“They want to be going out with a millionaire rockstar who is going to treat them like a princess and they're going to have a gorgeous life. And he's cool because he's in the Red Hot Chili Peppers, do you know what I mean?”

The Independent has contacted Kiedis’s representative for comment.

The rocker is currently dating podcaster Eileen Kelly, who is 33 years his junior. ​​Kelly defended their romance in April via a Vogue essay titled My Boyfriend is Double My Age.

open image in gallery The musician's current girlfriend, pictured in 2023 ( Getty )

“There is something to be said for a man who’s simply had more time to get his s*** together, and my much older boyfriend seems genuinely excited to be with me – not like he’s biding his time before he can swipe for someone better,” she wrote.

“Is it really so difficult to imagine that connection can exist across generations, and that two people of different ages can find something real in each other?” Kelly added.

A Reform councillor has been suspended after resurfaced social media posts appeared to show him calling for the Commons speaker to be hanged.

In response to a post about then-Commons speaker John Bercow, an account linked to Kirklees councillor David Rowan wrote on social media in October 2019: “Hang the Dwarf”.

In another post, which has not yet been deleted, the account also made homophobic comments, having said he doesn’t believe “gays should have kids full stop”.

A Reform UK spokesman said: "Cllr Rowan has been suspended from Reform UK pending investigation."

open image in gallery ( X )

Another post from Mr Rowan’s account also called for Westminster to be turned into a Wetherspoons, writing: “Think we should get our pick forks and whippets and demolish London.”

Mr Rowan, who was elected in May, also appeared to show support for far-right campaigner Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, known as Tommy Robinson, writing: “Thommy Robinson I salute you for caring.”

It comes as Nigel Farage continues to raise concerns about his own safety in the wake of the killing of Reform UK’s Ann Widdecombe.

open image in gallery Mr Rowan, who was elected in May, also appeared to show support for far-right campaigner Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, known as Tommy Robinson, writing: “Thommy Robinson I salute you for caring.” ( Kirklees Council )

Mr Farage has previously raised concerns about MPs’ security, including his own, and said after her death: “And I do fear that for anybody in public life, or especially the political space, things have become even more dangerous to them.”

The Reform UK leader said his party “had been treated very differently to everybody else” before the death of the former MP.

Counter-terror police investigating the death of Ms Widdecombe have now reopened a year-old probe into an alleged firebomb attack at Mr Farage’s home in south London, reports have said.

Officers said the incident, which the Telegraph described as a “lit incendiary device” being posted through Mr Farage’s letterbox, was reported in April 2025.

Asked about the probe, Mr Farage told reporters at a press conference earlier this week: “It’s a great, great tragedy that it took the death of Ann for the security services in Britain to finally take seriously the safety and security of Reform politicians and Reform prominent figures.

“Up until that moment, we had been treated very differently to everybody else.”

open image in gallery It comes as Nigel Farage continues to raise concerns about his own safety in the wake of the killing of Reform UK’s Ann Widdecombe. ( Reuters )

According to The Telegraph, Reform UK deputy leader Richard Tice pressed his panic button at his house last Christmas after being approached by an aggressive man outside parliament. Officers then made an arrest.

Reform UK MPs were given round-the-clock security protection, paid for by the party, after Widdecombe’s death over fears of similar attacks.

Reform UK spokesperson and former Tory minister Widdecombe died on 8 July after she was hit over the head with a hammer 21 times at her home in Haytor on Dartmoor, Devon, a court heard.

Joshua Kerry, 28, was charged with her murder on 20 July. He has not yet entered a plea and has been remanded in custody until his next court appearance.

More follows on this story...

News.title: Lidl’s launched a pastel-coloured kitchen range that looks just like Smeg’s
News.content:
The centrepiece of British kitchens. Smeg’s appliances are made to be admired just as much as they are to be used, bringing a pop of colour to everyone’s countertops. But let’s face it, they’re not exactly cheap.

Now, pastel fans, rejoice. Lidl’s about to launch a range of retro-inspired kitchen appliances that look exactly like Smeg’s, but cost a fraction of the price. Available in pink, mint and black, the range includes everything from kettles, toasters and microwaves to espresso machines, stand mixers and air fryers.

Coming to the middle aisle this weekend (Sunday, 16 September), here’s everything you need to know about Lidl’s range of retro kitchen appliances, and when you can get your hands on them.

What does Lidl’s pastel kitchen range include?

There’s a huge selection in Lidl’s new Pastel Kitchen range, but it’s the retro-inspired appliances that caught my eye. Most come in a choice of mint, pink or black, so you can mix and match, or just kit out your entire kitchen in green.

Lidl’s £16.99 kettle looks a lot like Smeg’s much pricier retro kettle, and comes in mint, pink and black. It has a stainless-steel body, a 1.7l capacity and a 3,000W heating element. Lidl says it can boil one litre of water in two minutes and 45 seconds. There’s also boil-dry protection, a removable limescale filter and a water-level indicator.

Lidl says its kettle can boil one litre of water in two minutes and 45 seconds ( Lidl )

The retro espresso machine is another highlight. It costs just £49.99 for Lidl Plus members and comes in mint, pink and black. It has a 15-bar pump, a portafilter with separate baskets for one or two shots, a 1l removable water tank and a swivelling steam wand for frothing milk or dispensing hot water.

I also love the look of Lidl’s £39.99 stand mixer, which comes in mint, pink and black. It has a 5l stainless-steel bowl and a 600W motor, and can mix, whisk and knead using planetary mixing action. It boasts digital speed controls, a turbo function and a runtime display, as well as a dough hook, whisk, flat beater and splatter guard.

And not to forget the humble air fryer. Lidl’s £29.99 air fryer comes in mint or pink. It features a large 4.7l capacity, with 3.6l of usable cooking space, and temperatures ranging from 40C to 200C. You can air fry, roast, bake, reheat, dehydrate and prove.

The coffee machine has a portafilter with separate baskets for one or two shots ( Lidl )

There’s also a 20l retro microwave that comes in mint or pink and costs £39.99 for a limited time. It has five power settings up to 700W and eight automatic programmes, as well as four defrost programmes, a quick-start function, child lock and an LED display.

In fact, there’s so much in the range that you’ll be shopping for hours. There’s a matching two-slice toaster for just £12.99, a £24.99 jug blender, a £17.99 mini chopper, a £14.99 milk frother and an £8.99 hand blender, all coming in pink, mint or black. Lidl’s even selling matching cookware and accessories, including £3.49 frying pans, £4.99 cake and loaf tins, £9.99 electric coffee grinders and £6.99 electric salt and pepper mills. You’ll also find pastel glasses, mixing bowls, kitchen utensils, food-storage containers and microwave cookware.

When can you buy Lidl’s pastel kitchen range?

Lidl’s pastel kitchen range goes on sale on Sunday 16 August, but as most middle aisle finds, once they’re gone, they’re gone. If you’ve got your eye on Smeg’s appliances, here are our tried and tested recommendations.

Smeg mini kettle Smeg’s mini kettle is much pricer than Lidl’s £16.99 variant, but if you want the original, you won’t be disappointed. “If you’re a fan of vintage gadgets, it’s highly likely this will be your dream model,” said Tamara Hinson in her round-up of the best kettles. “We’re big fans of its glossy finish and streamlined shape, as well as the speed with which it brought water to a boil, given its 1,400W of power.” £114 from Amazon.co.uk Prices may vary

Smeg EGF03 espresso coffee machine Lidl’s espresso machine looks exactly like this Smeg EGF03 coffee machine, but costs hundreds of pounds less. The original Smeg espresso machine can be used to brew espresso, cappuccino and lattes, with a double thermoblock heating system that it says allows for faster switch-on times and precise water temperature control. We’ve also tried Smeg’s cold brew machine, which isn’t exactly a lookalike of the more premium espresso machine, but our tester said “the integrated steam wand handled a range of dairy well”. £699 £600 from Harrods.com Prices may vary

For more, we’ve found the best coffee machines

News.content:

Jeremy Doku has signed a new five-year contract with Manchester City as he has become the fourth first-team player to agree a new deal this summer.

The winger, who had entered the last two years of his previous contract, will now stay at the Etihad Stadium until 2031.

He follows Phil Foden, Abdukodir Khusanov and Josko Gvardiol in agreeing to stay with City as their squad takes shape for the new season.

Doku, a £55m signing from Rennes in 2023, believes new manager Enzo Maresca’s style of play will suit him as he said it was an easy decision to remain with the FA Cup winners.

Doku said: “It's a privilege. I am so happy that they trusted in me first of all and as well that I can continue to play for this big club. I remember when I arrived here from France a bit of an underdog. Nobody really knew me. I had to prove myself and being able now to sign a new contract shows that they trusted me and that they appreciate how I've been playing.

“I'm very excited to work with Enzo. I've been watching the games the friendly games in Korea and the style of play is very attractive. But already when he was in his previous clubs, I saw this style of play, and it really suits me with the wingers being very aggressive.

“He demands a lot of us offensively and that's how I like it. So, I'm very excited to work with him and I believe me signing a new contract shows also he's trust in me and that's good.”

Director of football Hugo Viana added: “Jeremy is a huge talent whose improvement since joining us in 2023 is clear for all to see.

“He has a special dynamic. He has the right characteristics for what we are looking for in a winger. He really does bring a special quality to our team.

“Jeremy is also a fantastic person. He is someone loved across the club. His attitude is first class, and he wants to improve every single day.

“He deserves this new deal, and I know he will continue his improvement in the coming months and years.”

News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. Fidel Castro would have reached the age of 100 on Thursday, and his long shadow continues to cast over the island.

While he remains revered by some who miss him amid a severe US energy blockade, others view him as the architect of the system that brought about Cuba’s current crisis.

This week, Cuba marked Castro’s centenary through events such as the International Book Fair, art exhibitions, concerts and assemblies bringing together delegates from left-wing organisations across the continent.

Posters displaying his face are hung throughout hospitals, while road billboards feature his famous slogans — including his widely known "Homeland or Death". His presence remains so familiar that many Cubans simply refer to him as Fidel.

"I believe (Fidel Castro) leaves Cuba a legacy of dignity, morality, tireless work and concern for the poor," writer and essayist Miguel Barnet, who also is a member of the National Assembly, told The Associated Press. "And a philosophy that was translated into concrete policies in areas such as culture, education and public health."

open image in gallery Castro remains revered by some Cubans ( AP )

Castro’s centenary arrives as Cuba experiences an escalating economic squeeze that began when the Trump administration enforced a fuel blockade in January, subsequently introducing further sanctions intended to press the communist government into political and financial reforms. The measures have compounded a five-year economic slump triggered by previous US sanctions and a failed domestic monetary reform.

For ordinary Cubans, the impact has been severe: prolonged power cuts, shortages of fuel and medicine, declining industrial and tourist output, flight cancellations, transport limits and reduced working and school hours.

Castro ruled Cuba for nearly five decades, from 1959 until he transferred executive power to his brother in 2008, a tenure marked by huge public gatherings and speeches lasting several hours. He retained significant authority until his death in 2016.

"Fidel left us everything, everything good that came from Cuba’s revolutionary process," said Argelia Mustelier, a 61-year-old retiree who lives in Old Havana. "In these difficult times we’re living through, he would have found a way to bring some happiness to his country and his people."

Fidel Castro Ruz was born on 13 August 1926 in eastern Cuba’s sugar-growing region. His father, a Spanish immigrant, initially recruited labour for American sugar enterprises before establishing a successful plantation. After graduating as a lawyer, Castro quickly became politically active.

In 1953, Castro and more than 100 fighters launched an attack on the Moncada Barracks in Santiago de Cuba in a failed bid to depose dictator Fulgencio Batista. Captured and later released, Castro went into exile in Mexico before returning alongside fellow rebels to lead a guerrilla war that culminated in Batista’s overthrow in 1959 and Castro’s accession to power.

open image in gallery Some believe Castro is the architect of Cuba's current crisis ( AP )

Upon taking control, Castro radically reshaped Cuba through land redistribution, a national literacy drive and the nationalisation of private enterprises — policies that placed his government on a direct collision course with Washington.

Throughout Latin America and the developing world, Castro emerged as a symbol of anti-colonial and revolutionary movements. However, his policies also generated intense opposition, initially among wealthy Cubans who fled to the United States, and later among citizens resisting the Communist Party’s monopoly on political rule.

"He is a controversial figure," said historian Manuel Cuesta Murúa, president of the opposition Council for the Democratic Transition in Cuba.

"There was no justification for sacrificing freedoms… There was no justification for preventing the rest (of the Cuban people) — and the country’s political diversity and plurality — from expressing themselves," Cuesta said. "That created a rift whose consequences we are still living with today."

For many younger Cubans, Castro remains a historical icon, though his influence is less tangible than it is for older generations who lived through his leadership.

"Our generation didn’t experience him as an active leader. What we saw was a less visible Fidel, one who rarely appeared in public," 27-year-old Cristian Cohello said. "What remains of Fidel Castro right now, of what he left behind, is nothing; absolutely nothing."

Regarding the island's current situation, Cohello added that there is no solution: "Right now, even if they brought another Fidel, they wouldn’t be able to fix this."

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Advice, cookbooks and emergency pot noodles: Your best gifts for university students
News.content:
When it comes to sending a child or grandchild off to university, it can be tempting to fill their room with every conceivable gadget.

So to help, we asked the Telegraph Recommended Community for their best gift recommendations and their suggestions ranged from desk lamps to cookery books and supermarket gift cards.

Here are the essentials worth buying.

Kitchen basics

From cupboard essentials to electrical appliances and cookbooks, most readers say they’d gift kitchen equipment.

Thinking back to his university days, reader TJ, 43, from London, says “the main essentials are around kitchen items and good long lasting food”.

“It’s nice to have some bits to cook for others as well and to make friends quickly,” he adds.

Susan, 54, from the West Midlands, agrees, recommending “basic cooking equipment” as a key staple and “distinctive cutlery, plates and cups that are easily identified”, which are particularly useful for shared accommodation.

“A box of store cupboard ingredients such as olive oil, soy, stock cubes and spices to use when cooking,” is also well-received, she says.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

Team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register, or login to an existing, telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.

When you see a + in the tracker it indicates how many other games start at that time.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, one exception is this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football will launch in the two weeks leading up to the start of the Premier League. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

Sports.title: Bournemouth Dream Team preview: top stars, smart options & potential flops
Sports.content:
BOURNEMOUTH will participate in Europe for the first time in their history this coming season.

Andoni Iraola guided the Cherries to Europa League qualification before his move to Liverpool and Marco Rose has taken his place in the dugout at the Vitality Stadium.

PLAY DREAM TEAM NOW: £100,000 PRIZE POT!



Ahead of new the Dream Team campaign, let’s take a closer look at Bournemouth’s top stars, smart options and potential flops.



TOP STARS

First things first, Eli Junior Kroupi (£4m) would be the primary focus of this section if he was fully fit but, sadly, the gifted forward will not be available until November having undergone foot surgery in July.

Thankfully, he’s not the only talented 20-year-old in the squad as Rayan (£3.5m) deserves suitable recognition too.



Predominantly a right winger, the Brazil international is categorised as a midfielder in Dream Team but he may get some minutes through the middle as the season unfolds.

Rayan averaged a goal or assist every 160 minutes in the Premier League last season and so his output could go through the roof this term as he’s likely to be a guaranteed starter.

Another player who should benefit from a busier schedule is Adrien Truffert (£3.5m).

Bournemouth barely felt the departure of Milos Kerkez (£4.5m) because their new No3 hit the ground running and ensured left-back remained a position of strength.



The Frenchman featured in all 38 league games in 2025/26 and additional Europa League fixtures will give him a better chance of mixing it with defenders from Arsenal, Manchester City, etc.

Sports.title: Who is Mark Goldbridge and what is his real name?
Sports.content:
MADE HIS MARK Who is Mark Goldbridge and what is his real name?

MARK GOLDBRIDGE is a Manchester United superfan and influencer.

The social media star, who has amassed millions of followers online, has landed a deal with Disney+ to present their new Stick to United show with Wayne Rooney.



Who is Mark Goldbridge?

Mark Goldbridge rose to fame as a YouTuber known for the fan channel ‘The United Stand’.

He also has a separate channel called ‘Mark Goldbridge That’s Football’.



Goldbridge launched The United Stand in 2014 under the name Soccer Box TV, before later changing it to focus on Manchester United.

His entertaining outbursts about football and popular watchalongs – called by some as an “amateur online version of Sky Sports‘ Soccer Saturday” – saw him go viral online.

Goldbridge joined talkSPORT in 2022 and briefly hosted a late-night show.

He has also featured several times in the Sidemen charity match alongside social media stars like KSI.

In 2025, Goldbridge’s ‘That’s Football’ channel acquired the rights to show Bundesliga action and a year later his channels were purchased by The Overlap.

Disney+ has since acquired Gary Neville’s brand and will broadcast his Stick to Football show.



They will also launch a new Stick to United, which will be hosted by Rooney and Goldbridge.

What is Mark Goldbridge’s real name?

Born in 1979 in Nottingham, his real name is Brent Di Cesare.

He used to work as a police officer investigating financial fraud. He created the alias Mark Goldbridge when he began his YouTube career at the request of his employers.

Goldbridge explained: “When I started on YouTube my job would not have allowed me to use my real name.

“If you search the name Goldbridge I don’t think there’s anyone in the world with that name.”



What is Mark Goldbridge’s net worth?

Prior to him landing the Disney+ job, Goldbridge’s net worth is a reported £7million.

Sports.title: Fans think England finally have Harry Kane successor as Villa’s Brian Madjo, 17, explodes on to scene in Uefa Super Cup
Sports.content:
BRIAN MADJO’s Super Cup showcase has England fans convinced he can be the successor to Harry Kane for the Three Lions.

Madjo, 17, scored against Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain in his competitive debut for Aston Villa.



And now fans around the country are convinced the 6ft 4in teenager could grow into a world- class talent to finally solve England‘s fears around being able to move on from one of the game’s best attackers.

Despite the quality of the opposition, Madjo carved out a number of good chances that went begging, before finally getting on the scoresheet with an instinctive finish on the stroke of half-time.



Fans wrote on X while watching his performance: “Brian Madjo is going to be some player, 17 years old and he’s equalised against PSG for Aston Villa. We have our Harry Kane replacement.”

Another gushed: “That Brian Madjo is a problem. He’s one of those forces of nature that the only one that can stop him is him, so powerful.

“Reads the game in the box so well too, England might finally have a 9 after Harry Kane.”

A third fan claimed: “Yes this Madjo guy is mental he’s Kane’s replacement.”

And a fourth added: “Madjo to save England when Kane Retires.”

Madjo’s career has followed a bizarre trajectory so far, and even the ability for the Enfield-born star to play for England was briefly in question.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The 2009-born forward moved to Luxembourg at a young age with his family.

His father is Guy Madjo, a former Cameroon youth international who enjoyed spells with a number of English clubs including Crawley Town and Shrewsbury, as well as stints in China and Thailand.

Young Madjo began playing his football in Luxembourg, before making the switch to the academy of French side Metz in 2023.

He broke into the first team for the first time two years later, and made five appearances for the senior side before Villa swooped in with a £10million deal for the youngster in January.

But that signing proved to be far from straightforward due to a dispute over his registration.



The Villans believed that Madjo, who switched international allegiance to England in 2025 despite making three senior appearances for Luxembourg, would qualify as a home player when it came time to register him.

As well as already appearing for England U17, Madjo has UK citizenship, and it was anticipated that his signing would not be a problem.

But that was not the position of Fifa, who claimed he fell foul of their regulations that prevent clubs from making any international signings under the age of 18.



The club took the case all the way to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in a seven-month-long battle to clear the star to play in the UK.

And earlier this month their appeal was upheld, making Madjo eligible to feature in the Premier League and Champions League this season – much to the chagrin of any defenders in those competitions.

Madjo’s massive frame and power has drawn comparisons to Romelu Lukaku and Didier Drogba, but it is England talisman Kane that people clearly hope he will emulate.

Previous names touted as successors to the legendary Tottenham Hotspur and Bayern Munich forward have included Liam Delap and Madjo’s Villa team-mate Tammy Abraham.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

With the Euros at home in just two years’ time, fans will be desperate to see Madjo fill those very big boots.

Sports.title: Gold medallist Thomas chases 'own legacy' after AJ comparisons
Sports.content:
Commonwealth Games gold medallist Damar Thomas wants to create his "own legacy" after being compared to former Team GB super-heavyweight stars following his triumph in Glasgow.

The boxer followed in the footsteps of Joe Joyce, Frazer Clarke and Delicious Orie when he beat India's Narender Berwal via unanimous decision to win gold in the super-heavyweight category.

Standing at 6ft 6in, Thomas has earned inevitable comparisons with Anthony Joshua and represents one of the great hopes for the future of British heavyweight boxing.

The 21-year-old, who is targeting success at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, is unfazed by such comparisons and insists he is focused on his own development.

"Yeah, it's a great feeling [to win gold]. I managed to add my name to the British heavyweights that won the Commonwealth [gold]," he said.

Image: Thomas is aiming for gold at the LA Olympics in 2028

"Hopefully in LA I'll be able to add my name to those great heavyweights that managed to get Olympic gold.

Image: Thomas brushed off comparisons with Anthony Joshua

"I'm just in my own race at the minute and taking it in my own strides. I'm not comparing myself to anyone. I'm doing everything at my own pace, which is great. What I want to do is create my own legacy, which is a good feeling."

Thomas demonstrated significant boxing IQ in his 5-0 victory over Berwal, marking his 11th consecutive win in a run that extends back to November.

"My main asset is my feet and my speed," Thomas said.

"That's what works for me with these heavyweights, because a lot of these heavyweights rely on one shot. I don't rely on that, so it's great."

Image: Thomas has not lost a fight since November 2025

While Thomas' main ambition for now is to remain amateur and win gold in LA, he has his sights set on becoming a professional after the games in 2028.

"First, I want to tick off that box with LA. I'm taking one tournament at a time," he added.

"It's a marathon, not a sprint. And I'm just taking everything at my own pace.

"The main goal is the Olympics. Until then, I'm thinking about Olympics and nothing else. But after the Olympics, I'll definitely turn professional."

Spanish teenager Rafael Jodar's bid for ATP Tour rankings history was put on hold after he was beaten by Brandon Nakashima in the semi-finals of the Canadian Open.

Jodar, 19, had been hoping to make history in the Montreal for the fastest rise into the top 10 of men's tennis but his attempt to make a first Masters 1000 final was ended in straight sets by American Nakashima.

Nakashima, the 28th seed, had never previously made it past the third round at the tournament but was too strong for Jodar in a 7-6 (7-3), 6-4 triumph.

Jodar saved four match points before Nakashima finally converted his fifth to overcome the world No 15 in two hours and two minutes of play on IGA Stadium.

"Going into the tournament, I knew I was playing at a really high level, so I knew that I could get a go on a deep run here," said Nakashima.

"Obviously, wasn't thinking about the final or anything."

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Windsor and Lingfield feature on Thursday
Sports.content:
Windsor and Lingfield play host to Thursday evening's action - live on Sky Sports Racing.

7.41 Windsor - Law Court and City Of Poets head the field

Law Court and City Of Poets clash with an in-form trio in the RIP Susan Procter Memorial Handicap.

City Of Poets was building a progressive profile before slightly disappointing in the Coral Challenge on Eclipse day last month. He was partially hampered that day and the form of that race is very strong, so the drop back in class and step up in trip may see James Tate's representative bounce back to form.

A similar angle applies to Law Court, who ran on in a slowly-run competitive mile handicap at Glorious Goodwood and will certainly hold strong claims up in trip. His previous two showings at Sandown, which included a victory on Brigadier Gerard night, would give backers confidence going into this assignment.

In-form trio A Major Payne, Bold Impact and Parlando all won nicely last time out and remain on potentially handy marks, with the first runner winning in particularly taking fashion over the course and distance. That performance suggests the rise in class should not prevent him from staking a bold claim under Billy Loughnane, who is chasing his maiden jockeys' championship crown.

King's Code cannot be ruled out back down in class considering his Chester success last month, as Auld Toon Loon returns to his last winning mark over course and distance last August after finishing a creditable eighth in the John Smith's Cup.

Box To Box may find it tough on firmer ground after 11 months off the track, although he does remain on a competitive mark.

7.11 Windsor - Waterford Castle opposes Amo's expensive recruit

The highly-tried Waterford Castle pitches himself in calmer waters, facing Amo Racing's Partying - who was bought for 4.4m guineas - in the Matchbook Betting Exchange Supporting UK Racing Maiden Stakes.

The George Boughey-trained Waterford Castle is the only horse in here with a rating and comes to Windsor a 10-race maiden. The base form would suggest he is not very good but he has arguably just bumped into quite a few nice types in ultra-competitive races thus far.

His first two starts this year resulted in being turned over at odds-on, but the winner of the second contest won a valuable race at Sandown subsequently. This gelding finished second behind future Shergar Cup winner Archers Bay and managed to finish in mid-division in Royal Ascot's King George V Stakes - which reads very well given the winner Enceladus has since won a Group Three and the second Al Azd bolted up at Ascot next time out (earning a rating of 109).

The fly in the ointment could be Partying. This Frankel filly out of Aljazzi is an unknown quantity and should be watched in the market on debut. Of the others, Thatcham could be of interest returning from a break. Richard Hannon's charge was never in the race at Southwell the last day but could fare better on turf with Pat Dobbs booked.

7.28 Lingfield - Shangri La opposes Neswick

Shangri La opposes the eye-catching Neswick in Lingfield's Become a Friend of Racing Welfare Fillies' Novice Stakes.

The Kirsten Rausing-owned three-year-old bids to break her maiden tag following a creditable reappearance at Wolverhampton, where she placed fifth on handicap debut. This daughter of St Mark's Basilica could benefit from the step down in trip with Callum Shepherd in the plate. Her breeding suggests she will both do better at middle distances and develop with age and she sets the standard, dropping back into a novice.

The John and Thady Gosden-trained Dove Tale improved on her first start at three just a week ago, managing to place under Rab Havlin at Kempton. A half-sister to German Derby runner-up Diamond Dove, this filly could have more to offer.

Despite Neswick's modest pedigree, she shaped extremely well over course and distance on debut and can provide stiff opposition, especially if coming on for the run.
