Sports.title: Aston Villa boy wonder Brian Madjo can be Harry Kane’s England replacement despite playing for different country three times
Sports.content:
Aston Villa boy wonder Brian Madjo can be Harry Kane’s England replacement despite playing for different country three times

England fans might have been given a glimpse into the future watching Brian Madjo's memorable debut for Aston Villa.

The Villans were beaten 2-1 by Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Super Cup, but the Premier League side will be buoyed by the performance of their 17-year-old goalscorer in Salzburg.



4 Madjo took just 45 minutes to open his Aston Villa account Credit: Getty

Desire Doue netted the winning goal for PSG, as he fired the European champions back in front in the 61st minute.

Kvicha Kvaratskhelia had given the French giants an early lead, before Madjo became the main talking point of the first half.

Having signed for Villa for £10 million in January from French club Metz, the teenager was only recently cleared to play after a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling.



This saw Madjo handed his debut for the Super Cup, and he was immediately in the thick of the action, as he missed a series of glorious chances to equalise.

But his persistence was rewarded on the stroke of half time, as he guided a brilliant close-range volley into the net from John McGinn's cross.



This sparked huge celebrations from the Villa players, as Madjo entered his name into the record books.

At 17 years and 212 days old, the debut goal saw him become the youngest goalscorer in Super Cup history.



And while Madjo has three senior caps for Luxembourg, England fans will be thrilled to discover that he is very much in contention to become a star of the future for the Three Lions.

How can Brian Madjo still play for England?

Born in London, Madjo moved to Luxembourg at a young age, and got his first taste of international football with the European nation.

He represented Luxembourg at Under-15 and Under-16 level before making his senior debut in March 2025.

4 Could England fans be seeing more of Madjo after his standout debut for Aston Villa? Credit: The FA via Getty



And while Madjo has since gone on to take his senior caps tally to three appearances, his international future doesn't appear to lie with Luxembourg.

That is after he opted to switch allegiance to England in September 2025, as he received his first call-up to their Under-17s.

His change in international allegiances is permitted thanks to FIFA's eligibility rules, which have notably seen Declan Rice and Jack Grealish change their national teams.

This allows players who have featured in no more than three competitive matches before turning 21 are able to change nationalities.



But for Madjo, all three of his appearances for Luxembourg came in friendlies against Sweden, Switzerland and Slovenia last year.

This leaves him free to represent his country of birth, in what could now be a hugely encouraging sign for England fans.

4 England will need to consider life after record goalscorer Harry Kane at some point Credit: Getty

With no apparent long-term successor to 33-year-old talisman Harry Kane, Madjo could stake his claim as he looks to lead the line for Villa this season.



The teenager showcased huge physical pressure for a teenager against PSG, as well as taking up goalscoring positions.

His debut goal in the Super Cup saw him follow up on his impressive pre-season debut against Walsall, where he netted twice in a 5-0 win.

His prowess has long been known in Luxembourg, where he first made a name for himself in the Racing Union.

So much so in fact, that the club's academy director Delvin Skenderovic recently told talkSPORT.com: "I think he reminds me a lot of Romelu Lukaku.



"I think he has quite a similar profile where he's able to keep the ball, he's strong with his head.

4 Lukaku has been named in both the Serie A and Premier League teams of the year Credit: Getty

"But I just think Brian will be a little bit faster than Lukaku."

Sports.title: Myles Lewis-Skelly keeps fans guessing with Arsenal goal celebration as Mikel Arteta responds to question on transfer speculation
Sports.content:
Myles Lewis-Skelly keeps fans guessing with Arsenal goal celebration as Mikel Arteta responds to question on transfer speculation

Mikel Arteta says Myles Lewis-Skelly being linked with other clubs is a 'good sign' after the Arsenal star's cryptic celebration on Wednesday night.

Lewis-Skelly appeared to send a message to Arsenal fans after his goal during a pre-season friendly at home to Como.



2 Lewis-Skelly appeared to send a message to Arsenal fans after scoring against Como Credit: Getty

It came a day after talkSPORT revealed the versatile youngster had been offered to multiple Premier League clubs by the Gunners.

The 19-year-old found the target against Como at the Emirates Stadium on Wednesday night to open the scoring in the first half.

Como later equalised through Martin Baturina before half-time as the match ended 1-1.



Arsenal message?

Although Arsenal went on to win 4-3 on penalties, it was Lewis-Skelly's goal celebration which caught the attention of the fans.

The teenager gestured to the home fans before being congratulated by his teammates.



Footage captured from the stands appeared to show him apologising as he held up his hands before making a heart gesture.

Lewis-Skelly also tapped the Arsenal badge on his shirt before walking back towards his own half.



His reaction to scoring follows rising speculation over a potential exit from the Premier League champions.

One fan asked: "Is he saying bye?"

Another added: "Myles Lewis-Skelly celebrates by apologising to the Arsenal fans before throwing up a heart with his hands. One of our own, forever."

While this decisive fan declared: "He is going nowhere."

Arteta addresses Lewis-Skelly reports

Despite being encouraged by his player being in demand, Arteta refused to divulge any details on where the player could end up before deadline day on September 1.

“He’s a very emotional player. Remember when he did all the gestures on the pitch. I am not going to talk about any speculation," Arteta said.



“If there is any speculation about our players it is a good sign, it means we attract attention and they are doing a good job.”

Lewis-Skelly's future

The England international, who can feature at both left-back and in midfield has been offered to clubs ahead of the transfer window closing.

Amongst those sides are top-flight rivals Manchester United and Chelsea. Clubs had already been made aware of Lewis-Skelly's availability earlier in the summer.

However, fresh contact was made following Arsenal's signing of Bruno Guimaraes. The Brazil midfielder joined the club from Newcastle United for £75million on Saturday.



Lewis-Skelly has four years remaining on his current deal in north London after signing a new contract last summer.

2 Chelsea and United are amongst the clubs Lewis-Skelly has been offered to Credit: Getty

Having graduated from Arsenal's famed Hale End academy, he has already made 75 appearances for the club.

Of those, 20 came in the Premier League last season as the Gunners won their first title for 22 years.



Having played 62 minutes from the start against Como, Lewis-Skelly will hope to feature in Sunday's Community Shield.

Arsenal face Manchester City in the season's traditional curtain-raiser at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff on Sunday.

Lewis-Skelly has started all four of his side's pre-season fixtures so far this summer.

As well as his goal against Como, he also provided an assist for Max Dowman in a 4-1 win over Girona earlier month.

Sports.title: Cristian Romero takes big step towards Atletico Madrid transfer despite Tottenham agreeing fee with Serie A club
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid have agreed a deal in principle to sign Cristian Romero for a fee worth £34million, talkSPORT understands.

The Tottenham captain has long been tipped for a summer exit from north London, and Spurs had already agreed a fee with Napoli for the defender.



5 Romero's time at Spurs looks to be up Credit: Getty

The Serie A club were set to pay £34m for Romero, but were unable to agree terms with the player.

More recently, Romero was linked with a shock switch to Spurs' bitter rivals Arsenal, although any chance of this now looks to have ended.

While Inter Milan also held talks earlier with him in the summer, the Argentine is now set to get his dream move to Spain.



With a fee now agreed for him to join Atletico, Spurs will also retain a 15 per cent sell-on clause on any future transfer.

This comes after Romero agreed personal terms with LaLiga giants Atletico with the player to sign a four-year deal which has the option of a further year.



Romero is now set to join up with compatriot Diego Simeone at Atletico, in a move that will bring to an end his five-year stay at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

His expected £34m move also means that Spurs will make a loss on the £43million they paid Atalanta to sign Romero in 2021.



Tottenham's defensive overhaul

Spurs have signed centre-backs Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi this summer, with Micky van de Ven in positive talks over a new five-year deal.

This left Romero free to leave the club, despite penning a contract extension through to 2029 last August.

His imminent exit comes after he drew criticism from fans for his conduct and ill-discipline last season.

5 Romero now looks set to join Diego Simeone and his Argentine contingent at Atletico Madrid



Romero was sent off twice in 23 league appearances, and received ten yellow cards as Spurs narrowly avoided relegation.

The 2022 World Cup winner also became embroiled in a storm in May when it was reported that he was to miss Tottenham's crucial final game of the season in favour of a return to his homeland to watch formative club Belgrano.

With Spurs at risk of relegation and Romero getting wind of fan disgruntlement, he later changed his mind and instead was on hand to support his teammates in their quest for survival.

'Get rid of him'

As Romero closes in on a move away from north London, talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara had no qualms about Tottenham losing their captain.



Discussing the defender's links with Arsenal last week, the Sport Bar host and former Spurs player insisted the club would be better off without him, and claimed their new arrivals are better options.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, O'Hara said: “Get rid of him. I've heard there’s Arsenal chat about him - get rid of him.

5 The Argentine seeing red became a frustratingly familiar sight for Spurs fans in recent seasons Credit: Getty

“He was a liability for us last season. We’ve finished 17th in the last two seasons - he was the captain. He didn't want to be there on the last day. It was only because he got told that he had to come back that he ended up coming back.



“So get rid of him. We've got better players now. He's a liability.

“Van de Ven - make him captain. He's a player that you want in your side. You got Senesi, Van Hecke. Romero isn't even going to play.”

After two disappointing league campaigns, Tottenham have set about kickstarting a new era under Roberto De Zerbi this summer.

Spurs have splashed the cash in a bid to rebuild, spending £237m in total which includes twice breaking their club transfer record - first to sign Mateus Fernandes and then Sandro Tonali from West Ham and Newcastle respectively.

And O'Hara insisted there is no place for Romero in De Zerbi's new-look team, even after playing a central role in Argentina's run to the World Cup final.



5 Van Hecke looks set to fill Romero's boots after his £52million arrival from Brighton Credit: Getty

5 Romero helped Argentina through to a second consecutive World Cup final this summer, but his best form has often eluded him at Spurs Credit: Getty

Continuing to blast Romero, he added: “I'm happy to see the back of him.

"We need a new era under De Zerbi and it looks like he's putting a right good team together. We'll see what happens, but it looks like we've got a right good team and the players seem to like him.



“But Romero isn’t part of it. Get rid of him, get as much as we can."

Sports.title: Referee ends Manchester United vs Leeds friendly early
Sports.content:
Normal time of Manchester United's friendly against Leeds United was ended early after a string of pitch invaders disrupted the match.

The pre-season clash at Croke Park in Dublin was the first ever club football match at the iconic venue but was marred right at the end when multiple fans ran onto the pitch.



3 United's clash with Leeds was ended early after a pitch invasion by six supporters Credit: Getty

As the clock ticked down towards the 90th minute, a young supporter cleared the advertising hoardings.

Play was immediately stopped before five more fans invaded the pitch to take selfies with the players.

Whilst the TV cameras panned away from the incident, cheers could be heard from the crowd as each supporter entered the field.



Due to the disruption, referee Neil Doyle blew the final whistle before play restarted, without any added time indicated.

Meanwhile, it was announced on the PA system inside the stadium threatening to stop the match again if there were any more pitch invasions.



With the score level at 1-1, a penalty shootout followed once the pitch invaders had been removed.

United win on penalties

And the bragging rights belonged to Man United as they emerged victorious in the shootout, winning 5-4.



The decisive moment saw Noussair Mazraoui score the winning penalty after James Justin struck the crossbar with his effort.

United had appeared in control of the shootout after summer signing Harry Wilson was denied for Leeds by Dermot Mee.

However, an uncharacteristic miss from Bruno Fernandes as he sent his spot-kick wide resulted in sudden death efforts.

3 United beat Leeds on penalties to win the BOYLE Sports Cup Credit: Getty



The Red Devils captain's blushes were spared, though, after Youri Tielemans and Mazraoui found the target.

In doing so, United also get their hands on a piece of silverware by lifting the BOYLE Sports Cup.

Joshua Zirkzee had opened the scoring during the first half in the Irish capital.

His 16th minute strike made history as the first-ever club goal scored at Croke Park in its 142-year existence.



The match was the first association football match of any kind played at the 82,300-capacity stadium for 17 years.

Zirkzee's goal was cancelled out before half-time as Brenden Aaronson levelled for Leeds.

3 Zirkzee scored the first-ever club football goal at Croke Park Credit: Getty

When do United and Leeds play next?

United will now conclude their pre-season schedule against AC Milan on Saturday.



The two sides meet at the Wroclaw Stadium in Poland this weekend.

Michael Carrick's side then begin their Premier League campaign away to newly-promoted Hull City on August 22.

As for Leeds, they host Augsburg at Elland Road on Saturday before visiting Nottingham Forest on the opening weekend of the season.

Sports.title: Jeff Stelling predicts 2026/27 Premier League table and tips shock side for relegation
Sports.content:
Jeff Stelling has made his predictions for the 2026/27 Premier League season, including a surprise tip for relegation.

The new campaign gets underway next Friday (August 21) with champions Arsenal hosting newly promoted Coventry.

2 Mikel Arteta's Arsenal will be aiming to retain their Premier League title Credit: Getty

That's the first of 380 top-flight games to be played between then and May, with plenty of twists and turns inevitable.

But Stelling has already put his neck on the line by naming his picks for the title, European qualification and the drop.

Predicting the full Premier League table on talkSPORT, Stelling backed Arsenal to retain their title with Chelsea as runners-up, followed by Manchester City in third and Manchester United in fourth.

He placed Tottenham fifth – which has been enough for Champions League qualification in each of the last two campaigns – and Liverpool sixth, with Newcastle seventh and Aston Villa eighth.

Fulham to fall?

However, perhaps Stelling's most eye-catching prediction came at the bottom end of the table, where he felt Fulham would go down.

Joining Stelling on air, Peterborough chairman Darragh MacAnthony and former Villa striker Gabby Agbonlahor voiced their conerns over Fulham.

As well as Alvaro Arbeloa replacing Marco Silva as head coach, the Cottagers have lost key players this summer such as Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez.

Between them, Wilson and Jimenez accounted for more than a third of Fulham's Premier League goals last term.

"We called it as well, like two weeks, three weeks ago, didn't we, about Fulham," noted Agbonlahor. "We agreed that that's our team that could be under pressure..."

Stelling believes that Fulham could be in "big, big trouble" in the upcoming campaign.

2 Arbeloa is one of nine new Premier League managers for the start of the 2026/27 season Credit: Getty

The Cottagers' ostensible replacements for Wilson and Jimenez are youngsters Cesar Palacios and Gonzalo Garcia, both of whom have followed Arbeloa from Real Madrid.

And while striker Garcia scored six LaLiga goals at an average of just over one every 30 minutes last season, it remains to be seen how he'll fare in the more testing environment of the Premier League.

Fulham face a tough-looking opening fixture when they host West London rivals Chelsea on Monday, August 24.

Stelling positive about Sky Blues

While he tipped Fulham to be relegated alongside newly promoted Ipswich and Hull, Stelling joined MacAnthony in backing last term's Championship winners Coventry to survive – putting them 15th in his table.

Justifying his decision, he said: "Coventry...spent a lot of money – not on a huge number of players actually. They've chosen quality over quantity.

"Scored a lot of set-plays last season and that could be big for them again this season."

Sports.title: Premier League pre-season friendly descends into chaos with a penalty taken against an OPEN GOAL after Fulham walked off in row over new manager Alvaro Arbeloa's red card
Sports.content:
Premier League pre-season friendly descends into chaos with a penalty taken against an OPEN GOAL after Fulham walked off in row over new manager Alvaro Arbeloa's red card

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Fulham's friendly with Malaga on Wednesday night was that in name only after an acrimonious ending after the full-time whistle, which included new manager Alvaro Arbeloa being sent off.

The Cottagers drew 2-2 at their Spanish opponents - with the hosts claiming a draw courtesy of Eneko Jauregi's 90th-minute penalty after Calvin Bassey was penalised for a handball.

However, that's where the drama started...

With the match ending in a draw, Malaga's players were preparing for a penalty shootout to determine who would win the Costa del Sol Trophy.

But there was one sticking point... Fulham's players were not and instead headed down the tunnel, sparking boos from the home supporters.

It led to some confusion on the pitch as Eneko picked up the ball and rolled a penalty into an empty net to ironic celebrations from him and his team-mates and the majority of the 17,179 fans inside La Rosaleda.

🎬⚽️ Absolute cinema! During a pre-season friendly between Malaga and Fulham that ended in a 2-2 draw, the La Liga club was ready to do a penalty shootout, but Fulham left the field saying a shootout wasn’t in the friendly contract.



So a Malaga player took one in the empty net… pic.twitter.com/mF2qX5eHVx — Ultras Clips (@ultras_clips) August 12, 2026

Fulham's players refused to take part in a penalty shootout after drawing 2-2 at Malaga

In a bizarre ending to the match, Malaga ended up winning the Costa del Sol Trophy

Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa was sent off after full-time as he was unhappy with the referee

After the match Fulham released a statement explaining why they didn't partake in the shootout, writing on X: 'Thank you for your excellent support in Malaga this evening!

'We can confirm that prior to the match, both teams agreed that there would not be a penalty shootout in the event of a draw.'

According to beIN Sports, Fulham also didn't get involved in a shootout as it could affect their travel plans.

If that incident wasn't enough there was also the small matter of Arbeloa's dismissal who was unhappy with the referee at full-time.

As official Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias blew for the end of the game, Arbeloa made a beeline for him before being shown a red card.

Spanish outlet Marca was damning of Arbeloa and Fulham's actions, writing: 'This was a deplorable act of disrespect and an unprecedented lack of respect in the history of the Malaga friendly.

'During the break to decide who would take the penalties, Arbeloa clashed with referee Ortiz Arias and was shown a straight red card.

'Amid the ensuing chaos, Fulham decided to leave the field and refuse to participate in the penalty shootout, in one of the most embarrassing incidents in the history of football in Malaga.'

Sports.title: Turkish giants Galatasaray make audacious move to sign Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli - as Gunners set asking price for Brazilian
Sports.content:
Galatasaray have made their move for Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli with a £38million offer.

However, the Brazilian is not inclined to leave for Turkey.

The 25-year-old is one of the players Arsenal are prepared to listen to offers for with a valuation around £50m.

Roma have also shown interest and it is understood Martinelli will only consider options from the strongest leagues.

Arsenal are re-evaluating options to strengthen their left hand side.

They are also continuing discussions with Aston Villa for centre back Ezri Konsa with their latest proposal understood to be around £40m for the centre back.

Galatasaray have made their move for Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli with a £38million offer

Martinelli has been an ever-present at the Emirates over recent years after joining from Brazilian side Ituano as an 18-year-old in 2019.

Now 25, the forward has played 278 times for the club, scoring 62 goals, including 11 strikes in 53 appearances last season.

However, Martinelli struck just once in the Premier League, and of his 30 top flight appearances, only 11 were starts, with Mikel Arteta often preferring to use Eberechi Eze and Leandro Trossard on the left.

His most productive campaign was 15 league goals in 2022-23 and the Gunners have already added left-sided attacker Christos Tzolis this summer.

Speaking earlier this week on what we can expect from Arsenal over the rest of the transfer window, Arteta said: 'There is more that we want to do.

'Because every time we have an opportunity to improve the squad and bring more quality and depth, we need to do that.

'We’re actively trying to do so – the thing is, in the market, it doesn’t just depend on you, and we’re very clear on that.

'The will and the desire of the club is unquestionable, but we cannot promise that we’re going to do it because it doesn’t only depend on us.'

He added: 'For the margins to improve, there are very few players in the market that are available to do that and bring more quality to the club. But again, we’re actively looking to improve that and we’re going to try.'

Sports.title: Lionel Messi plays first game for Inter Miami since father's death... after devastated star hinted he could QUIT soccer in emotional tribute
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi played his first game for Inter Miami since the death of his father on Wednesday night.

The soccer star's father Jorge died at 68 on August 7 following a battle with illness that overshadowed the Argentina captain's mesmerizing World Cup campaign in the United States, in which he led his team to the final.

The devastated forward came onto the pitch in the 46th minute of Inter Miami's clash with Club Leon in the Leagues Cup tournament pitting MLS and Liga MX sides against each other.

Messi received a standing ovation from the audience at the Nu Stadium as he entered at halftime. His substitution had a positive impact on the side, but The Herons fell 3-2 to Leon.

The result officially eliminated Inter Miami from the knockout stages of the tournament, following their win over Atletico San Luis and a prior loss to CF Monterrey. Inter Miami reached the final of last year's tournament and won the 2023 edition of the Leagues Cup.

For Messi, the match was his first since the death of his father. It also came on the same day the Argentine posted a heartbreaking tribute on his Instagram account.

Lionel Messi made his return to Inter Miami days after the death of his father

Lionel's father, Jorge Messi, passed away on August 7 following a long battle with illness

Messi was a second-half substitute, but couldn't help Miami overcome a 3-2 loss to Club Leon

'Dad, I still can't believe you're gone,' the tribute read in Spanish. 'It hasn't sunk in yet, or rather, I don't want to accept it. It's very difficult for me to imagine never seeing you again, never talking to you again.

'I know you were suffering and that this is for the best, but you left too soon. We still had so much to enjoy together.

'I don't know what I'll do without you, I don't know how to go on. I only played football and now I have serious doubts that I'll continue doing that for much longer.

'You were by my side from the beginning, it was so close to the end. Why couldn't you hold on that little bit longer and we could have finished together?'

Longtime sporting rival Cristiano Ronaldo replied to the post, saying: 'A huge hug to you and yours in these tough times, Leo. Much strength.'

The Portuguese legend knows of Messi's heartache only too well after losing his father, Jose Dinis Aveiro, in 2005 to an alcoholism-related liver condition when he was aged just 20.

'I really don’t know my father 100 per cent,' Ronaldo told Piers Morgan in 2019. 'He was a drunk person. I never spoke with him, like a normal conversation. It was hard.'

Messi revealed that his father was the driving force behind his decision to play at this summer's World Cup, but his ageing legs prevented him from bringing the trophy home – with Spain winning 1-0 in the New York final.

Lionel Messi has thanked fans for their support following the death of his father Jorge (left)

Messi's father and agent died in Rosario, Argentina on Friday August 7

Jorge's death saw an outpouring of emotional tributes from the football world, including from Messi's first team Newell's Old Boys, as well as Barcelona and Argentina.

'You kept asking me to play in the last World Cup, and just a few days before it started, you got worse,' Messi's tribute continued. 'It was the first time you wouldn't be in a tournament, but Mom kept telling me you'd get better and be well enough to travel. I told you we were going to reach the final so you could travel.

'Every time a game ended, I waited and missed your message. That's when I realized the situation was really serious. Even so, I couldn't stop thinking about going as far as possible, to give you time and for you to see a game. We reached the final and you couldn't be there. I wanted to win it to bring it to you and show you a new one. I couldn't, my legs couldn't take it anymore. This time I tried to go against my physical limitations, but I couldn't. I never managed to feel well.

'When I arrived, you thought we'd lost the final on penalties. We couldn't talk about anything that happened. You couldn't enjoy any of it. We didn't win the championship, but you don't know how much we enjoyed every game. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play.

'I'm telling you this because it was the only thing we couldn't talk about, because you already know everything else. We used to talk every day and see each other whenever possible, given my commitments.'

Messi missed Inter Miami's defeat by Monterrey on Sunday to return home in the wake of his father's passing, and thanked fans for their well wishes.

He added on his Instagram stories: 'I want to sincerely thank everyone for all the love, respect and enormous consideration you have shown me and my family during this incredibly painful time following the loss of my dad.

'Thank you for being there for us, for every message, every gesture and, above all, for respecting our grief and our privacy.'

Lionel Messi's father Jorge, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, died at the age of 68

MESSI STATEMENT IN FULL 'Dad, I still can't believe you're gone. It hasn't sunk in yet, or rather, I don't want to accept it. Messi also posted a picture with his father, captioned: 'I love you, pa' in Spanish.

Football legend Messi was extremely close to his father, who also operated as his agent and de facto business manager throughout his career, overseeing his son's multi-million dollar empire off the pitch.

In recent months, though, the patriarch of the family had been dealing with an as-yet-unconfirmed medical issue that had seen him taken to hospital in his home country.

His illness first came to light when Lionel, 39, cried on the pitch at the World Cup in a rare public display of emotion.

After scoring a hat-trick against Algeria in Argentina's opening group game in Kansas City, Messi was questioned by journalists and said: 'No, honestly it's something completely unrelated to sports. It's been a few difficult days, complicated.'

Just hours later, journalist Eduardo Feinmann explained the reason for the tears in an interview on Radio Mitre, one of the country's most listened-to stations.

'This has to do with his father. His father is not in good health,' he said. 'For quite some time now, several months, since last year.

'And this week there were some situations that slightly worsened his health, and Messi is going through this internal struggle. In other words, like any human being.'

Messi stands in front of his family (including father Jorge (third left) in Rosario in October 2003

It has since been reported that Jorge suffered a 'medical episode' at his home in January of this year, and he was hospitalised as a result.

In the aftermath, he was said to have undergone cardiovascular and neurological tests, but no official diagnosis was shared by the family, who sought to keep Jorge's health out of the media.

Jorge's health became headline news again in June, when a broadcaster in Argentina falsely claimed he had died – before later issuing an emotional apology and stepping down from her job.

Lionel is the third of four children of Jorge and his wife Celia Cuccittini, and the pair remained together until his death.

They married in 1978 and split their time between Rosario and Miami, where their footballing superstar son currently plays for David Beckham's Inter Miami in Major League Soccer (MLS).

Before becoming Lionel's agent, Jorge worked for a steel manufacturer in Villa Constitucion, meeting his wife as a young man in Rosario – where the family then grew up.

Jorge arrives at son Lionel's wedding in 2017 with his wife Celia (L) and daughter Maria (R)

Messi has two older brothers, Rodrigo and Matias, and a younger sister, Maria Sol.

Jorge has been at Messi's side throughout his historic career, which began in Argentina with Newell's Old Boys, before he moved to Spain to join Barcelona's famed La Masia academy in 2000.

He became the greatest of all-time in an incredible 21 years in Barcelona, before stunning the world with a move to Paris Saint-Germain – orchestrated by Jorge – in 2021.

After two seasons in the French capital, he moved to MLS and Inter Miami, where he remains to this day at the age of 39.

While Lionel's career has been magical on the pitch, it has not been without controversy off it, with Jorge famously by his son's side throughout his tax fraud case in 2016.

The pair sat together in front of the court, with Jorge in his role as his son's business manager, with the prosecution alleging that Messi failed to properly pay tax on income from his image rights between 2007 and 2009.

Ultimately, both father and son were convicted of three tax offenses, initially each receiving suspended 21-month prison sentences.

Jorge's sentence was subsequently reduced to 15 months upon review in 2017 by Spain's Supreme Court, with the pair also hit with substantial fines.

Sports.title: How Man City will replace Rodri - and the inconvenient truth for World Cup hero that shows they might be better off without him
Sports.content:
Rodri is due in Manchester on Friday, after his planned back surgery following World Cup glory meant he was given two extra days' holiday. But in the context of that rehabilitation and the harsh reality that his future now lies away from Manchester City, it wouldn’t represent a great surprise if the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner did not return to the building for regular pre-season testing.

City are braced for yet more haggling with Barca and want to recoup more than £60million for a central midfielder in the final year of his contract, who was awarded player of the tournament last month. Somebody who often looked physically shot last season, yet was imperious at international level.

There is a balance to strike for director of football Hugo Viana in making sure City maximise Rodri's value while also realising that this orchestrated exit – heavily signposted for a year and solidified by Pep’s Guardiola goodbye, with the 30-year-old starting only 18 Premier League games in the last two seasons – likely only ends one way.

Guardiola called it last autumn, that City would not see the best of his metronome all season and that recaptured form would be reserved for the World Cup. The suggestion felt intriguing at the time, more by the way in which it was delivered – a little knowing, somewhat resigned. City’s medical staff were attempting to curb Rodri’s desire to to rush various injury comebacks.

There are those who believe his performances Stateside, when temperatures dictated that games were played at a slower pace, prove that there is still nobody better across Europe than him. But in finally coming to terms with a parting of ways, City may look at diminishing returns: in the past two seasons, City win fewer matches when Rodri starts.

In the Premier League, the win ratio is exactly half with him starting. Without, it is 60.3 per cent. A very similar story plays out from 29 starts in all competitions. Never before in Rodri’s City career have the team won more games in his absence.

Manchester City are braced for yet more haggling with Barca and want to recoup more than £60million for Rodri, who was awarded World Cup player of the tournament last month

But in finally coming to terms with a parting of ways, City may look at diminishing returns: in the past two seasons, City win fewer matches when Rodri starts

Although not an exact science – City still always concede fewer goals when he’s the deep midfielder – and a small sample size, it does represent a comparison worthy of note.

City, and Enzo Maresca, would prefer to plough on with him, of course. Their movements in the transfer window paint a picture of how this is only heading one way.

Proactive and forceful club denials around interest in Chelsea’s £120million-rated Enzo Fernandez at the beginning of the summer have now given way to silence. Fernandez wants to reunite with his old boss Maresca and those close to him believe the feeling to be mutual. Ayyoub Bouaddi, the Moroccan who lit up the World Cup, is edging closer to signing from Lille, as the French club demand £85million.

City sources say Bouaddi's arrival is not linked to Rodri’s future and that they are pursuing him regardless of what happens, in a window that is threatening to become busy if Tijjani Reijnders and potentially another midfielder leave.

Yet his displays across almost 100 senior games, earning rave reviews for a physicality off the ball and intelligence on it, dictate that he can be ready to impact City’s fortunes. His minutes will have to be carefully monitored and managed.

What seemed apparent on Wednesday, when Elliot Anderson was unveiled to supporters during an event at the Etihad, was that the £116million club-record signing fancies more of a roaming ‘box-to-box’ role than filling Rodri’s void.

‘I’ve spoken to the manager a few times – he explained the sort of things that I need to do,’ said Anderson. ‘There is a lot of running, a lot of energy. It’s to try and control games. That is what I can do.

‘I’ll see where I get used. Creating things, driving forward or the other role if they ask me to do that. Kevin De Bruyne was always the player I looked up to over the last 10 years. I loved watching him. To be here at the same club and playing where he played is special.’

Ayyoub Bouaddi (right), the Moroccan who lit up the World Cup, is edging closer to signing from Lille, as the French club demand £85million

There is a feeling that Enzo Fernandez (left) wants to reunite with Enzo Maresca, but for now Elliot Anderson (right) is the man City have identified as the one to run their midfield

City identified Anderson's aggression and punch in the pass as ideal for the way the Premier League operates these days. Maresca has operated with a two-man midfield in his pre-season fixtures – Mateo Kovacic and Reijnders against Atletico Madrid in South Korea on Sunday – and in that system, Anderson would appear as the one who springs forward, chipping in with the sort of goal he scored away at City during a 2-2 draw in March, arriving late.

Kovacic is ahead of Nico Gonzalez in the pecking order and expected to start Sunday’s Community Shield against Arsenal in Cardiff. Both Gonzalez and Kovacic have publicly declared that they do not wish to leave this summer.

The physical demands Maresca places upon his midfielders is huge, with Phil Foden or Rayan Cherki vying for the role pushed up alongside Erling Haaland. Maresca is looking at around half a dozen options as part of the two, with that second runner crucial. The way Reijnders crashed the boxes during their friendlies showcased exactly what is being preached on the training pitch.

‘I’ve taken take huge confidence knowing that I can perform on a World Cup stage,’ Anderson said, also admitting that he’s still struggling with England's semi-final defeat by Argentina. ‘Obviously I hadn’t played in anything as big as that yet. I had a big decision to make on who to join and I’m confident I’ve made the right one.’

Sports.title: LIV Golf's demise takes another blow as embattled tour tells players $40m season finale is CANCELED... despite still pushing ticket sales
Sports.content:
After weeks of speculation, LIV Golf has officially informed its players that the season finale in Michigan has been canceled. It appears, however, this has not been relayed to the ticket sales department.

Reports at the end of July hinted that the LIV Golf Michigan Team Championship was set to be scrapped, denying the 13 teams playing on the rebel circuit the chance to compete for the $40million prize.

According to The Telegraph, that decision is now official as players have been told the event is now off.

While an official announcement has not yet taken place, the outlet reports that Fox has removed the tournament from its TV listing and no infrastructure had been built at the course set to hold the event: The Cardinal at Saint John's.

This means that next week's tournament, LIV Golf Indiana, will be the final event of the 2026 season for LIV Golf after the Saudi Public Investment Fund announced it would no longer be funding the rebel circuit after this season's conclusion.

Despite the information being relayed to the players, emails from LIV Golf continued to advertise ticket sales for the Michigan event.

James Corrigan of The Telegraph posted a screenshot of said promotional email with the subject line 'Get your tickets for Aramco LIV Golf Michigan Team Championship 2026 - Grounds before they're gone!'

LIV Golf has informed its players that the $40m Team Championship has been canceled

However, it appears the rebel tour is continuing to advertise ticket sales to the Michigan event

The future of LIV remains uncertain after the Saudi PIF announced they were backing out

Comments underneath Corrigan's post claim LIV Golf doesn't show the Michigan event on their schedule anymore, however, users could still purchase tickets if they click on the link sent through the email.

It's yet another cancellation made in the wake of the PIF's pullout. Back in June, LIV Golf Louisiana was canceled.

This comes at a time where the future of the breakaway circuit continues to be shrouded in uncertainty.

Scott O'Neil, the chief executive of LIV, revealed last week that an investor had been lined up to fund the league's operations in 2027.

However, the identity of said investor has not been officially revealed and no agreements appear to have been signed.

Reports indicate that the deals hinge on keeping golf stars Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm in the roster.

The conclusion of the season now remains a mystery. It's not clear how the team race will be decided at the Indiana event, with players telling The Telegraph that they 'remain in the dark' on how a winner will be determined and whether the $40million in team prizes will be distributed.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick offers clear indication Marcus Rashford will STAY at Man United: Star in manager's plans as forward prepares for return to action against the man who exiled him
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick offers clear indication Marcus Rashford will STAY at Man United: Star in manager's plans as forward prepares for return to action against the man who exiled him

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Marcus Rashford could make his first appearance since returning to Manchester United against AC Milan on Saturday – managed by Ruben Amorim, the man who bombed him out in the first place.

The England international has returned from a loan spell at Barcelona and is now intent on fighting to regain his place at Old Trafford.

He has been told he’s in Michael Carrick’s plans after United’s draw with Leeds in Dublin. By a quirk of fate, it is against Amorim’s Milan side that he will make his return, after an extended post-World Cup break.

Bryan Mbeumo led the line again here and got the assist for Joshua Zirkzee’s goal, but Carrick said of Rashford: ‘He’s our player. He’s come back great. He’s just like any other player... He gives us something a little bit different.’

The summer has been as much about evolution as it has been revolution, with the results of the Mbeumo striker experiment yielding some fascinating results.

The Cameroon international, 27, is far from your typical No9 but for Carrick, that is a big part of his appeal.

Marcus Rashford is in Michael Carrick's plans after his return to Manchester United

United want to give academy star Shea Lacey some space in the first team and he predominantly plays off the right. There is also Amad Diallo, who is facing a defining season in that right-side role. Then you must add in the fact United only have one orthodox No9 option, Benjamin Sesko, and he hasn’t kicked a ball during pre-season due to a shin injury – although he did travel to Ireland to take part in this week-long training camp. Rashford could nudge himself ahead of the Slovenian.

Mbeumo as a striker, and a fluid one at that, holds great appeal and perhaps importance, especially if United do not sign another striker before the September 1 transfer deadline.

Mbeumo’s goals dried up in the second-half of last season and he struggled to rediscover the momentum that had United fans off their seats in the first-half of the campaign.

It led to questions over how Carrick could get the best out of him. But his double against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm, the equaliser in Gothenburg against Paris Saint-Germain and a brilliant piece of skill, coupled with an assist, for Zirkzee to open the scoring here against Leeds in Dublin showed just how much confidence is running through Mbeumo’s veins.

For the opening goal – and he should have had one of his own in the first half when he crashed a shot against the crossbar – he nutmegged two Leeds players as he burst down the left before playing Zirkzee through to score beyond new No1 James Trafford.

Leeds went on to equalise through Brenden Aaronson in the first half and were good value for it after a rocky start.

Despite Carrick’s side dominating the ball when their main men came on, it finished 1-1 in front of an 82,000-strong sell-out crowd at Croke Park. United won 5-4 on penalties.

Mbeumo is set to start as a centre forward at Hull City to kick-start United’s Premier League campaign on August 22. From there the sky feels like the limit for him. This is a formula now, not just an experiment.

Sports.title: The encouraging signs emerging under Michael Carrick's coaching, Bryan Mbeumo passes latest No 9 audition - and the young star the club CANNOT afford to let go as Man United beat Leeds on penalties
Sports.content:
Manchester United edged out rivals Leeds United on penalties to win the pre-season Boyle Sports Cup inside a sold-out Croke Park.

While the shootout - which almost didn't happen due to a deluge of young pitch invaders at full-time - ultimately separated the sides, both managers will have taken plenty from this pulsating clash under the lights in Dublin.

Bryan Mbeumo's audition to be Manchester United's starting striker for the opening game of the season was strengthened with another smart display, while Brenden Aaronson finished off a brilliant move to level things up at 1-1 in the first half.

James Justin's costly penalty miss as the fifth taker for Leeds allowed Noussair Mazraoui to win it with the final act as Michael Carrick's side clinched the game 5-4 on spot-kicks.

Daily Mail Sport brings you some of the biggest talking points from an historic night in Dublin…

Joshua Zirkzee (left) and Bryan Mbeumo (right) starred as Manchester United took on Leeds

TRUST COACH CARRICK

One of the things that Ruben Amorim called for was time on the training pitch to imprint his ideas on the United squad.

They fluffed the Europe league final to secure a season without European football and bar a couple of encouraging flashes, tangible signs of style and progress never materialised.

So to see Manchester United playing as well as they have throughout this pre-season - yes, it's pre-season - is a sign of just what good training ground coaches Carrick and his staff are proving to be.

It's a collective effort between Carrick, Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans, Travis Binnion, and many analysts in the background.

Here against Leeds United, much as it was against Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg last weekend, you can see tangible signs of progress in the way Carrick wants this team to evolve in its pressing and its play-style.

'He wants to have the ball, he wants to press in certain ways,' summer signing Youri Tielemans explained on Tuesday.

'It might be different than what you are used to, what I have been used to before, but it is logical things in my opinion. It is just smelling football, and that is what I have been doing from when I was young at Anderlecht, you know. So for me, nothing changes, but it just needs to gel together.'

United are proving a lot more aggressive in the press and the defensive work of Andrey Santos in midfield, one of the summer signings to the tune of £50million, is pivotal.

The encouraging thing is that while these haven't been perfect performances either, there are more first team stars to come back in.

United lit up Croke Park from the start without captain and talisman Bruno Fernandes, without Tielemans, without Matheus Cunha, without the returning Marcus Rashford, without Benjamin Sesko, and Matthijs de Ligt, and Harry Maguire.

The way Leeds picked United off, capitalising on loose control from Tyler Fletcher, shows that there is still work to do.

But stylistically United, visibly at least, appear to be getting better by the game. For Manchester United fans, that's an incredibly encouraging sign.

Throughout pre-season you can see exactly what Michael Carrick is trying to implement

MBEUMO ON A HEATER

In a summer at Manchester United which has been as much about evolution as it has been revolution, the results of the Bryan Mbeumo striker experiment are yielding some fascinating results.

The Cameroonian is far from a typical No 9 but for Michael Carrick and Manchester United's staff, that is a big part of his appeal.

There are a multitude of factors at play here. United want to platform academy star Shea Lacey for a full-time first team role and he predominantly plays off the right. There's also Amad, who is facing a defining season in that right-side role.

And then you add in that United only have one orthodox No 9 option in Benjamin Sesko, and he hasn't kicked a ball during pre-season due to an ongoing shin injury, although he did travel to Ireland to take part in this week-long training camp.

So Mbeumo as a striker, and a fluid one at that, holds great appeal and perhaps importance, should United not go and add another forward between now and the transfer deadline.

Mbeumo is going to start the season up top, that now looks clear, but expect Carrick to call upon Marcus Rashford, too.

'He's our player,' he said last night. 'He's come back great. He's just like any other player... He gives us something a little bit different.'

Mbeumo hit a real lull in front of goal in the second half of last season and struggled to rediscover momentum that had fans off their seats in the first half leading to question marks about how Carrick may get the best out of him.

But a brace against Atletico Madrid in Stockholm, the equaliser in Gothenburg against PSG, and a brilliant piece of skill, coupled with an assist, for Joshua Zirkzee to open the scoring here in Dublin showed just how much confidence is running through Mbeumo's veins right now.

For the opening goal here - and he should have had his own in the first half when he crashed a shot against the crossbar - he nutmegged two Leeds players as he burst down the left before playing Zirkzee through to score beyond new No 1 James Trafford.

Leeds went on to equalise through Brenden Aaronson in the first half and were good value for it after a rocky start. Despite Carrick's side dominating the ball when their main men came on, it finished 1-1 in front of an 82,000-strong sell-out crowd at Croke Park.

Mbeumo is set to start as centre forward against Hull City to kickstart the Premier League campaign and from there the sky really does feel like the limit for him. This is a formula now, not just an experiment.

TYNAN TIME

While he didn't quite get the loudest cheer of the night - that was reserved for the introduction of Bruno Fernandes off the bench - this was a huge milestone in the career of Tynan Thompson.

The 18-year-old arrived from Tottenham Hotspur this summer as an Emerging Talent Signing that Ineos and United's powers love, look at Ayden Heaven and numerous others.

This was Thompson's first taste of senior football at United and the first time he's been away and part of Carrick's group this pre-season.

Tynan Thompson got his first taste of senior football in a Manchester United shirt in Dublin

Thompson, who arrived in a deal that could eventually total £8m, got a pep talk from his manager moments before the second half restarted and the message, likely, was to be bold, be aggressive and have fun.

What we saw across 45 minutes was a player who looks unafraid to take people on and, in something of a quirk in the modern game, is a winger that likes to take people on on the outside.

A couple of times midway through the second half he managed to get down the left side with a quick burst and then drill a low cross in, only for Leeds to mop it up comfortably.

Sources at United won't pigeonhole Thompson as a first team player or an Under-21 player and he's likely to find himself straddling the two.

But don't underestimate the value of nights like these, in front of 82,000, with the likes of Fernandes and Cunha demanding the ball off you.

This isn't academy football any more…

HARRY'S STYLE

Speaking of rising stars, it should be an impossibility that Harry Amass is allowed to leave unless United go out and get another left back.

Sources have indicated that Amass has been told his best chance of regular minutes will come elsewhere and the club are unlikely to stand in his way for a loan or a permanent, if they get fair value.

That plan needs shelving immediately unless someone like Lewis Hall, who United have made two approaches for but failed on both occasions, walks through the door.

Amass may physically be on the smaller side in stature but he was dynamic in possession and fierce out of it here as Leeds looked to put him under real pressure, particularly early on before they clocked that they may be better off testing Diogo Dalot instead.

Amass has suitors aplenty should he walk out the door but with only Luke Shaw to call on as a bonafide left back right now, Amass should be staying until further notice.

There is no way Harry Amass can be allowed to leave without a new left back coming in

TRAFFORD IS TOP

One thing that Leeds do deserve credit for is the decisiveness they have shown in the goalkeeper department in getting a top talent in James Trafford.

They gave it as long as they could with Illan Meslier, then tried Lucas Perri out, and pivoted to Karl Darlow, now of Manchester United, before paying a club record £40m for him.

Officially Trafford got the Man of the Match here before it went to a penalty shootout and he did make a number of fine saves to keep Manchester United out, not least denying one effort from Zirkzee, and another from Mbeumo.

It cannot be understated just what a difference a truly top goalkeeper can make and if Leeds are to kick on like Brighton and Bournemouth did in getting into Europe, it is moves like Trafford that will go a long way to moving the needle.

MAKE IRELAND A YEARLY TRIP

Lastly, a sold out Croke Park was absolutely incredible, and a trip United should make yearly if the logistics were feasible.

The appetite for Manchester United in these parts is understandably huge and credit as well to the Leeds United contingent who travelled in good numbers.

Naturally the pre-season appeal is wherever the money is for Premier League clubs and the answer for Manchester United is often the United States.

But they could do a lot worse than secure themselves a near-enough home game in Ireland given how many fans turned out for this one.

A cracking trip that should give United's execs pause for thought.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
